question: Why is the CI pipeline structured as a funnel where unit tests run before behavioral tests?
options: Unit tests produce more detailed error messages than behavioral tests
GitHub Actions requires jobs to run in alphabetical order
Behavioral tests cannot run unless unit tests generate the required test fixtures
Cheap, fast tests run first and fail fast, saving time and LLM API costs on broken commits before expensive tests run
explanation: Structuring the pipeline as a funnel means cheap tests (unit tests that take seconds and cost nothing) run first. If they fail, the pipeline stops immediately without running expensive behavioral tests that require LLM API calls. This saves both time and money on broken commits.

question: Why does the regression check job use the condition 'if: github.event_name == pull_request'?
options: Regression checks need access to the base branch which is only available on pull requests
The full regression evaluation is expensive (requires many LLM calls), so it only runs on PRs to main to control API costs
Regression checks only work on pull request branches
GitHub branch protection rules require this condition
explanation: The full regression evaluation suite makes many LLM API calls and takes longer to run. Running it on every push to every feature branch would be prohibitively expensive. By limiting it to pull requests to main, you get regression coverage where it matters most (before merging) while controlling costs.

question: How do branch protection rules and the CI pipeline work together to gate deployments?
options: Branch protection rules automatically deploy code when tests pass
Required status checks in branch protection prevent merging to main until all CI test jobs pass, and deployments only trigger on pushes to main
Branch protection rules replace the need for CI test pipelines
The CI pipeline sends results to branch protection which then decides whether to deploy
explanation: Branch protection rules require status checks (Unit Tests, Behavioral Tests, Regression Check) to pass before a PR can merge into main. Since the deployment workflow only triggers on pushes to main, and main is protected, only code that has passed all tests can reach deployment.
